oil.summary: Crude markets staged a volatile session defined by geopolitical whiplash. Brent flash-crashed more than $6 intraday — from $107.24 to $100.80 — before recovering toward $104, as conflicting signals emerged from U.S.-Iran peace talks that Tehran quickly dismissed. WTI settled marginally lower at $96.25 (-0.23%) while Brent shed nearly 1% on the day, though both remain sharply higher on the month. The diplomatic noise drove a week-long Brent decline of nearly 9%. On the supply side, the U.S. temporarily eased Russia sanctions to cap the price surge, drawing European pushback, even as Ukraine struck a Russian oil terminal in St. Petersburg with over 1,000 drones. BPCL purchased 1 million barrels of U.S. WTI, Rystad cautioned Hormuz flows are unlikely to fully normalize before mid-2027, and the Dubai benchmark slipped into contango for the first time since July — a structural signal that Middle Eastern supply is beginning to exceed near-term demand. Distillates outperformed, with heating oil surging 2.63% and RBOB gaining 1.31%.
drivers: U.S.-Iran peace talk speculation triggered a $6 Brent flash crash before Tehran's denial forced a partial recovery
U.S. temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions added bearish supply sentiment, partially offset by Ukraine drone strike on St. Petersburg oil terminal
Dubai benchmark slipping into contango and Rystad's warning that Hormuz flows won't normalize until mid-2027 point to a bifurcated near-term supply picture
sources: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged up 1.58% on the day to $2.901/MMBtu, extending a solid weekly gain of 7.56%, though the contract remains under pressure on a one-month basis (-5.38%). The dominant macro story is the IEA's warning that a global gas crunch could persist well into 2027, with European storage at the lowest level in over a decade heading into the heating season. Against that backdrop, the Trump administration's push to restore Russian gas transit through Ukraine to the EU — widely reported by the WSJ — added a potential bearish supply catalyst, though no deal has been concluded. On the LNG side, ADNOC Gas signed a five-year deal to supply up to 1.6 million tons to TotalEnergies, and Shell sold its 16.67% stake in Australia's North West Shelf LNG project to the UAE's XRG for $1.45 billion, signaling continued Gulf state consolidation in global LNG infrastructure.
drivers: IEA warning of a prolonged global gas crunch through 2027, with European storage at decade lows, underpins near-term bullish sentiment
Trump administration pushing to resume Russian gas flows to Europe via Ukraine — if successful, would represent a material bearish supply shift for the continent
Gulf state LNG consolidation accelerates: ADNOC Gas locks in five-year TotalEnergies supply deal while XRG acquires Shell's North West Shelf stake for $1.45 billion

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs dipped modestly to $85.66 (-0.56%) on the day but remain firm on the week (+2.19%) and month (+7.32%), consistent with elevated energy market stress feeding through to carbon demand. Dedicated power sector news flow was thin today. The most notable development was Drax unveiling a £20 billion AI data centre plan at its North Yorkshire biomass site, a significant pivot that raises questions about future biomass power generation capacity and grid interconnection at the facility. Brazil's data centre policy outlook was also flagged as contingent on gas regulations and grid access following its recent election. Iran's claim that Hormuz could reopen within two days if U.S. demands are met adds a tail-risk variable to European power fuel costs, though Tehran's track record of follow-through on such statements is poor.
drivers: EU EUAs hold month-long gains above $85 as elevated fossil fuel costs and supply uncertainty sustain carbon demand from power generators
Drax's £20 billion AI data centre announcement at its biomass plant signals a major potential shift in site utilization and grid demand dynamics in the UK
Iran's conditional Hormuz reopening offer, if realized, could ease fuel input costs for gas-fired power generation, though credibility remains low
sources: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
